data.note: Probe only files on the base; exit 4/5 or 0 tests is unavailable, never 'not failing'

data.body:
Fixes bug B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran: The baseline command passes a test file that exists only on the branch (here tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py). Replayed on main f8c6444f5: pytest exits 5, "no tests ran", 0 executed. The gate recorded baseline red=false, still_failing=[] and called all 40 failures "new failure(s) not failing on main", while running those same 40 without the branch-only path on main gives 39 failed, 1 passed. A red baseline is hidden and a clean branch is blamed; the verdict is drawn from a run that executed nothing. Fix: drop paths absent from the base, and treat exit 4/5 or 0 tests run as unavailable, never as not failing. Found on fix-B-review-identity-from-worktree-ignores-as-agent.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran --regression-test <test>` first).

Scope found while reading: the cause is testselect._without_test_locations keeping a test path absent from the probe tree; pytest exits 4 (5 under xdist, which hides the ERROR line) and every id stays unmeasured, which gate_baseline then calls new. A branch-only NODE in an existing file aborts a chunk the same way, so it is handled too, or a genuine new failure would turn unavailable. A gate unavailable over real failing tests must not be auto-answered by the standing complete_unavailable rule: guarded at its one call site in complete/approval.py (services/approvals/policy.py is leased by fix-approvals).

data.claim: The probe aborts because testselect._without_test_locations keeps a test path absent from the base tree; under xdist pytest then exits 5 and names nothing, while `-n 0` names every missing node without running a test.
data.falsifier: Real pytest with -n 2 and an unknown node id runs the known ids, or `-n 0` does not print ERROR: not found.
data.mechanism: `location` required (root/t).exists(), so a branch-only file in a narrowed command survives into the base command. _chunk returns None for that run, on_base keeps red=False, still_failing=[], and gate_baseline's `fresh` is every id.
data.probe: pytest -q tests/test_a.py::test_a tests/test_nope.py ; pytest -q tests/test_a.py::test_a tests/test_a.py::test_new ; pytest -q -n 2 tests/test_a.py::test_a tests/test_b.py::test_q ; same with trailing -n 0 ; then BR.on_base with run_command_gate on a scratch repo (.venv pytest 9.1.1 + xdist)
data.probe_output: missing file: 'ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_nope.py', no tests ran, rc=4. missing node, serial: 'ERROR: not found: .../tests/test_a.py::test_new (no match in any of [<Module test_a.py>])', rc=4. Param: test_p[9] printed as test_p. Under -n 2: 'no tests ran', rc=5, no ERROR line. With trailing -n 0: 'ERROR: not found: .../tests/test_b.py::test_q', no tests ran in 0.00s. on_base after the fix: still_failing=[test_a, test_p[1]], unmeasured=[], red=false, branch-only file never run; calls exit 5, 4, 1, 5, 4, 1.
data.question: Why does the baseline probe read a run that executed nothing as 'not failing on the base', and can pytest itself say which ids the base lacks?

evidence.note: R-baseline-probe-no-tests-ran CONFIRMED: real pytest 9.1.1 exits 4 on a missing path or node, exits 5 silently under -n 2; -n 0 names the node with no test run

chunk_findings.detail: `_no_verdict` only checks `ran < asked` for exit codes in `CUT_SHORT`; for a normal, non-CUT_SHORT pass it returns `False` whenever *any* test executed (`outcome == "passed" and not ran`). That means a run that reached and executed one of `asked` IDs is treated as a complete verdict for every requested ID. If the generated pytest command keeps a selection option such as `-k` or `-m`, pytest can execute only a proper subset of `part` while returning a pass. For example, with `part = ["test.py::test_a", "test.py::test_b"]` and a pass whose only executed test is `test_a` (`summary=["1 passed"]`, exit 0), `ran` is 1, so `_no_verdict` returns `False`; `_verdicts` then records `test.py::test_b` as `False` even though it never ran. That ID is then counted as not failing on the base, yielding a false new failure. `asked` should be honored for all exit classes, or an ID not reached must remain unmeasured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py _no_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: The new setup invokes `git` directly via `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` instead of going through the project adapter, violating [r-adapters]. The rule requires every external dependency such as git/subprocess tools to have one port in `ddflow/adapters`; tests should use the fake adapter. These lines execute the real git binary directly, so they bypass the adapter and are not isolated from the host git availability/configuration.

chunk_findings.detail: The new location test only recognizes a nonexistent test **file** via `is_test_file(t)`; it still misses a branch-only test **directory** such as `tests/new_suite`. For `_without_test_locations(["tests/new_suite"], base_root)` where `base_root` has no `tests/new_suite`, `(root / t).is_dir()` is `False` and `is_test_file("tests/new_suite")` is `False` for a directory, so the path is kept. The generated base probe then runs pytest with a nonexistent directory plus the selected base files, pytest aborts with “file or directory not found” before running any selected file, and the gate gets no verdict/unavailable instead of measuring the base files and keeping the branch-only tests as new failures. This is the same no-tests-ran shape as the branch-only file case the change intended to fix, but for directory selections.

chunk_findings.detail: When all `todo` ids are branch-only, `_run_chunks` marks them `False` and sets `rest=[]` before it ever checks whether `gdef.command` is pytest. If the command is not pytest, the `for` loop body never runs, so `_probe` never returns `NOT_PYTEST`; the function returns `([], [], {id: False})` as a normal measurement. `on_base` then returns `red=False, unmeasured=[]` for a non-pytest gate. This violates the requirement that a non-pytest command has no probe and stays failed as documented. Input: `gdef.command` is not pytest, and the only failing id is a file present in the branch `tree` but absent from the base checkout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_run_chunks

chunk_findings.detail: A base run where the asked test is skipped is now treated as "no verdict" instead of measured false. If the base output is `outcome == "passed"` with summary `1 skipped`, the count `ran` from `EXECUTED` is 0 (`skipped` is not executed), so `_no_verdict` returns `True` for a single asked id. `_lacking` finds no "not found" name and returns empty, so `_probe` returns `seen={}` and `on_base` reports `unmeasured=[id]`. The correct baseline verdict is that the skipped test did not fail on the base, so it should be a measured new failure rather than making the gate unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_no_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: A branch-only test directory is still kept when the base tree lacks it. Given `root` is the base checkout and `args=["tests/new_feature/"]` where that directory exists only on the branch, `(root / t).is_dir()` is False and `is_test_file(t)` is False, so the function does not treat `tests/new_feature/` as a test location and leaves it in the returned command. The base probe then runs pytest against a nonexistent directory, which pytest rejects before running any tests—the same branch-only abort this change is meant to prevent. That can turn a branch-only directory into a no-measurement/false baseline failure instead of probing only files present on the base.

chunk_findings.detail:
The new test helper invokes git and a subprocess directly:
`subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "add", "-A"], check=True)` and
`subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "commit", "-qm", "narrowed"], check=True)`.
This bypasses the required adapter port for external dependencies (git and subprocess tools) described in [r-adapters]. In an environment without a real `git` on PATH, or when the adapter-backed fake is expected, this helper does the wrong thing; the rule says these dependencies must go through `ddflow/adapters` so tests can use a fake instead of a real subprocess/git.

In a hermetic test environment where the real `git` binary is replaced or blocked, these fixtures now fail before exercising gate logic, so the test suite is no longer isolated from the host.

data.body:
Fixes bug B-baseline-bug-not-filed-silently: gate_baseline._file returns "" whenever bug_found exits non-zero, so the ci gate of fix-B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran recorded 30 ids measured red on e01cd49e2 with found.bug='' and reason '..., bug not filed'. The refusal is swallowed: neither the evidence nor the output says why no bug exists, and D-baseline-red-auto-accept requires the bug filed or linked. Found on fix-B-baseline-branch-only-test-no-tests-ran.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-baseline-bug-not-filed-silently --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-baseline-bug-not-filed-silently --regression-test <test>` first).
